steps: Boil a kettle and start the noodles in a large saucepan, cooking for 4 minutes or per the packet, then drain.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, so they are easy for a toddler to chew.
Cut the red peppers into thin short strips and grate or slice the carrots into thin matchsticks, 4–5cm long at most.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots and cook for 3 minutes, then add the peppers for 2–3 minutes until soft enough to squash between your fingers.
Stir in the soy sauce diluted with 45ml water, toss through the noodles, and cut them into short lengths before serving.
pitfalls: Using the full amount of undiluted soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water.
Leaving long noodles and big strips whole is a choking risk, so cut everything into short, small pieces.
Undercooked chicken or hard carrot is unsafe or tough for little ones, so cook the chicken until no pink remains and the carrot is soft.
output.tip: Let the stir-fry cool for a few minutes and check a piece yourself before serving, as peppers and noodles hold heat.

steps: Boil a kettle and bring a large pan of unsalted water to the boil for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, and cut the red peppers into short, thin strips.
Cut the carrots into thin matchsticks or grate them coarsely so they soften quickly and are easy for a toddler to chew.
Cook the noodles for 3–4 minutes until soft, drain, then snip into short lengths with kitchen scissors.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat, then stir-fry the chicken for 4–5 minutes until white all the way through.
Add the carrots and peppers and fry for 4–5 minutes until soft, then toss in the noodles with the soy sauce diluted with a splash of water.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of undiluted soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and taste.
Cutting the vegetables too thick leaves carrot hard and tricky to chew, so slice thin or grate.
Overcrowding the wok steams the chicken instead of searing it, leaving it pale and rubbery, so cook in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Cut the chicken and noodles into small, manageable pieces and let the stir-fry cool until just warm before serving to a toddler.

steps: Boil a full kettle and start the egg noodles in a large saucepan, cooking for 4 minutes or per the packet.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, then cut them into small bite-sized pieces.
Peel the carrots and cut them into thin matchsticks; slice the red peppers into small, thin pieces.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots and cook for 3 minutes, then add the red pepper and cook for 2 minutes until soft enough for a toddler.
Drain the noodles, toss them into the wok with the soy sauce, then cut the noodles shorter with scissors before serving.
pitfalls: Leaving the carrot in thick pieces keeps it hard and creates a choking risk, so cut it thin and cook until tender.
Adding the full amount of soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so add it a little at a time and stop when lightly coated.
Undercooking the chicken strips is unsafe, so cut a thick piece open to check it is white throughout.
output.tip: Dilute the soy sauce with a splash of water before adding it, so it coats everything evenly with less salt.

steps: Fill the large saucepan with water and bring to the boil over high heat for the spaghetti.
Finely chop the onion and garlic while the water heats.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the beef mince over high heat, breaking it up until browned, about 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt the boiling water and cook the spaghetti for 10–11 minutes until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so use high heat and let it colour.
Burnt garlic turns bitter and spoils the sauce, so add it only for 1 minute before the mince.
Rinsing the spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water over low heat for 1 minute so it coats every strand.

steps: Boil a kettle and put a large pan of well-salted water on the hob.
Finely chop the onion and garlic while the water heats.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the beef mince in two batches, 5–6 minutes each.
Lower to medium heat, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper, then simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 1 minute less than the packet time, reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan makes the mince steam and turn grey instead of browning, so cook it in two batches.
Burnt garlic turns bitter, so add it only after the onion has softened and cook for no more than 1 minute.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce will not cling; drain it and do not rinse.
output.tip: Toss the spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water over low heat for 1 minute so it coats every strand.

steps: Fill the large saucepan with salted water and bring to the boil over high heat.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and crush the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the beef mince, breaking it up and browning over high heat for 6–8 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the spaghetti for 9–10 minutes until al dente, reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so use high heat and let it colour.
Burnt garlic turns bitter and spoils the sauce, so add it only after the onion has softened and stir constantly.
Draining the spaghetti without saving any pasta water leaves a sauce that is too thick to cling, so keep a mugful back.
output.tip: Finish the spaghetti in the sauce for 1 minute with a splash of pasta water so it absorbs the flavour.

steps: Bring a large pan of water to the boil on the hob, then season it with the salt.
Cook the spaghetti for 1 minute less than the packet time.
While the pasta cooks, drain the tuna and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over low–medium heat, then add the tuna for 1–2 minutes.
Scoop out 100ml of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the spaghetti with the tuna and a splash of pasta water over low heat for 1 minute, until glossy.
pitfalls: Overheating the tuna dries it out and makes it chalky, so only warm it through.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the spaghetti dry and clumpy, so keep some to loosen it.
Under-salting the cooking water leaves the pasta bland, as the tuna and oil cannot make up for it.
output.tip: Warm your serving bowl under the hot tap first so the pasta stays hot while you eat.

steps: Bring a large pan of water to the boil over high heat and add the salt.
Cook the spaghetti for 1 minute less than the packet time, stirring in the first 30 seconds to stop it sticking.
While the pasta cooks, drain the tuna if tinned and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over low–medium heat, then add the tuna for 1–2 minutes, just until warmed through.
Scoop out about 100ml pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the spaghetti in the frying pan with the tuna and a splash of pasta water for 1 minute, until glossy.
pitfalls: Overcooked spaghetti turns soft and breaks up when tossed, so keep it al dente and finish it in the pan.
Frying the tuna on high heat or for too long dries it out and makes it chewy.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the dish dry and oily, because the starchy water is what binds the sauce.
output.tip: Season the pasta water well, as it is the main source of seasoning for the spaghetti.

steps: Bring a large pan of water to a rolling boil on the hob and add the salt.
Add the spaghetti and cook for 1 minute less than the packet time, stirring in the first 30 seconds.
While the pasta cooks, drain the tuna if tinned and flake it with a fork.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over low heat for 1 minute.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the spaghetti, tuna and a splash of pasta water in the pan for 1 minute, until glossy.
pitfalls: Cooking the tuna over high heat dries it out and makes it chalky, so only warm it through.
Draining away all the pasta water leaves the spaghetti dry and sticky, so keep a mugful to loosen it.
Under-salted cooking water leaves the pasta bland, as the tuna and oil cannot make up for it.
output.tip: Taste a strand 1 minute before the packet time; it should have a slight bite at the centre, as it finishes cooking in the pan.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, then heat the oven to 220°C and rub the beef with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and cook 50–60 minutes for medium (60°C in the centre).
Parboil the peeled potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain, shake to roughen the edges, then roast in hot oil on a tray for 60 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the batter of flour, eggs, milk and salt, then rest it for 30 minutes while the potatoes roast.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the Yorkshire tin for 10 minutes, pour in the batter and bake 20–25 minutes.
While the puddings bake, roast the carrots and parsnips with butter for 30 minutes, steam the broccoli for 4 minutes, and simmer the stock and wine with the roasting tin juices for gravy.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so keep it shut for the first 20 minutes.
Putting batter into lukewarm oil gives flat, greasy puddings, so the oil must be smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for at least 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the beef's resting time as your oven window for the Yorkshire puddings, and keep the carved meat covered in foil with a tea towel to hold its heat.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, then heat the oven to 220°C. Rub the beef with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and seasoning.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and cook 1 hour 10 minutes for medium. Rest it for 30 minutes under foil.
While the beef roasts, peel and cut the potatoes and parsnips, parboil the potatoes for 8 minutes, drain and shake roughly.
Heat oil in the baking trays for 10 minutes, then roast the potatoes and parsnips for 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once. Peel and chop the carrots meanwhile.
Whisk the batter and rest it for 30 minutes. When the beef comes out, raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tin until smoking, then bake the puddings for 20–25 minutes.
Make the gravy in the roasting tin on the hob with red wine, stock and juices, then simmer for 10 minutes. Boil the carrots for 10 minutes and the broccoli for 3–4 minutes.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door during the Yorkshire pudding bake makes them collapse, so wait until they are deep golden.
Pouring batter into lukewarm oil gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it is smoking.
Carving the beef straight from the oven sends the juices running out and leaves it dry, so rest it for at least 30 minutes.
output.tip: Cook the beef to 55°C in the centre for medium, as it will rise a few degrees while resting.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking, then rub with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper, and preheat the oven to 220°C.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and cook 1 hour 10 minutes for medium (60°C core). Rest for 30 minutes under foil.
While the beef roasts, peel and cut the potatoes, parboil for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Heat oil in a tray, then roast at 200°C for 60–70 minutes, turning once.
Peel and cut the carrots and parsnips, toss in oil and butter, and roast on a second tray for the last 40 minutes.
Whisk the batter and rest it for 30 minutes. When the beef comes out, raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tin until smoking, pour in batter and bake 20–25 minutes.
While the puddings bake, steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes. Deglaze the roasting tin with red wine, add stock and the beef juices, and simmer 10 minutes to make the gravy.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so wait until they are deep golden.
Adding batter to tepid fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it is smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven sends the juices running out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Roughen the edges of the parboiled potatoes by shaking them in the colander for extra crisp roasties.

pitfalls: Cooking the chicken straight from the marinade in a crowded pan steams it rather than browning it, so brown it in two batches and wipe off excess yoghurt first.
Adding the tomatoes and simmering hard at a rolling boil can make the yoghurt on the chicken split and turn the sauce grainy, so keep it at a gentle bubble.
Cooking the rice without rinsing it first leaves it gluey and clumped; rinse 300g until the water runs almost clear, then cook it while the curry simmers so both finish together.
output.tip: Finish the curry with a squeeze of lemon juice and a handful of chopped coriander to lift the flavour and cut through the richness.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken straight from the marinade into a crowded pan steams it rather than browns it, so brown it in two batches over a high heat.
Pouring in the tomatoes without scraping up the browned bits leaves bitter, burnt flavour stuck to the pan, so deglaze with a splash of water as they go in.
Cooking the rice without rinsing it first leaves it sticky and clumped, so rinse 300g until the water runs clear and use about 600ml of water.
output.tip: Finish the curry off the heat with a spoonful of yoghurt, a squeeze of lemon juice and chopped coriander to lift the flavour and add freshness.

pitfalls: Adding the tomatoes to a pan with no deglazing leaves browned chicken and marinade stuck on the base, which can scorch and taste bitter, so scrape it up with the first splash of tomatoes.
Putting heavily yoghurt-coated chicken straight into the pan makes it stew rather than brown, so scrape off the excess marinade and brown the thighs in two batches.
Starting the rice only once the curry is simmering risks a rushed or cold side, so cook 300g of rice (rinsed, with about 450ml water) during the last 15 minutes of simmering.
output.tip: Stir in a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice at the end, then finish with chopped coriander, to lift the flavour of the shop-bought paste.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or adding them to the wok undrained, makes them gummy and clumpy, so soak until just flexible and drain well.
Crowding the frying pan with all the tofu at once drops the oil temperature and steams the cubes, so fry in two batches with 1cm of oil at about 180°C.
Adding the soy sauce straight onto the tofu or leaving the crisp tofu in the sauce for long softens the coating, so toss it through for under 30 seconds just before serving.
output.tip: Whisk the soy sauce with 2 tbsp of water and a little of the leftover cornstarch slurry so it thickens into a glossy sauce that clings to the noodles and tofu.

pitfalls: Cooking the rice noodles in the wok without soaking or boiling them first leaves them hard in places and gummy in others, so soak or boil them until just tender and drain well before adding.
Adding the soy sauce while the pan is still crowded and not hot enough makes the vegetables stew and the cornstarch tofu go soft, so keep the heat high and pour the sauce around the edge.
Leaving the broccoli in large florets means the stems stay raw while the tops overcook, so cut them into small, even pieces of about 2cm.
output.tip: Toss the drained noodles with a teaspoon of oil after soaking so they do not clump, and add a splash of water to the wok if the sauce reduces too quickly.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or adding them to the wok undrained, makes them gluey and breaks them up, so soak until just flexible and drain well.
Adding the soy sauce and noodles while the wok is overcrowded or wet steams the vegetables and leaves them limp, so keep the heat high and the broccoli pieces small and dry.
Stirring the crisp tofu back in for too long, or letting it sit in the sauce, turns the coating soggy, so toss it for no more than 30 seconds just before serving.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small, even florets and blanch or splash with 2 tablespoons of water and cover for 1 minute so it cooks through without the pepper going soft.

equipment: Suur kaanega praepann või madal hautuspott
steps: Pane veekeetja keema ja loputa riis külma vee all, siis hakkab see kiiremini keema.
Keeda riis kaanega potis kergelt soolatud vees (või täitsa ilma soolata), 12–15 minutit, ja lase kaane all puhata.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt, lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks.
Prae sibulat ja porgandit kuumal pannil õliga 4–5 minutit pehmeks, lisa kana ja prae 6–8 minutit, kuni liha on igast küljest valge.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8 minutit; soola lisa ainult napilt või üldse mitte, kuubik annab soolsust niigi.
Sega hapukoor kastmesse, soojenda 1–2 minutit ilma keetmata ja maitse enne serveerimist; väikesele lapsele võta oma portsjon enne mis tahes lisasoolamist.
pitfalls: Ära lisa soola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik on juba soolane ja roog läheb väikesele lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda hapukoort kastmes tugevalt: see lõheneb ja kaste muutub kokkutõmbunuks.
Ära praa kanatükke liiga kaua: filee kuivab ja läheb kummiseks.
output.tip: Kasuta vähem puljongikuupi (või lahjenda rohkem veega) ja maitsesta täiskasvanute taldrikul laual, siis saab laps samast potist vähemsoolast toitu.

equipment: Suur kaanega praepann või madal kastrul
steps: Pane veekeetja keema ja loputa riis külma vee all läbi.
Keeda riis kaanega potis pehmeks, umbes 12–15 minutit, ja lase kaane all puhata. Soola vette ei pane või vaid näpuotsatäis.
Haki sibul peenikeseks ja riivi porgand jämedalt, samal ajal kui riis keeb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm tükkideks ja prae kuumal pannil õliga kuldseks, 5–6 minutit.
Lisa sibul ja porgand ning hauta 5 minutit pehmeks. Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml keevas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit.
Tõsta pann tulelt, sega hapukoor sisse ja soojenda vaikselt läbi. Maitse enne lisasoola ja serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära lisa soola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik on juba soolane ja road läheb väikesele lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda hapukoort kastmes tugevalt: see hakkab kokku kerkima ja kaste muutub tükiliseks.
Ära prae kanafileed liiga kaua: liha kuivab ja muutub kõvaks.
output.tip: Kasuta puljongikuubikut pool kogusest ja lisa maitse lõpus ürte või musta pipart, siis saad vähem soola ka täiskasvanute maitse jaoks.

steps: Pane riis pesemata sõela alla ja loputa külma veega, siis keeda riis kaanega potis pehmeks, umbes 15 minutit.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt, kuni vesi riisipotis soojeneb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks ja prae kuumal pannil õlis 5–6 minutit, kuni liha on kergelt kuldne.
Lisa sibul ja porgand pannile ning hauta 5 minutit, kuni sibul on pehme.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile, sega hapukoor juurde ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit madalal kuumusel.
Maitse kaste enne soolamist, sest puljongikuubik on juba soolane, ja serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära soola kanaga enne puljongit: kuubik annab juba piisavalt soola ja roog läheb väikesele lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära lase hapukoorega kastmel jõuliselt keeda: hapukoor lõheneb ja kaste muutub tombuliseks.
Ära prae kana liiga tihedalt pannil: liha hakkab hauduma ega pruunistu.
output.tip: Kasuta vähem puljongikuupi või lahjenda seda rohkem veega ning lisa maitset sibula ja porgandiga, siis on roog väiksele lapsele sobivam.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja loputa hapukapsaid vajadusel, kui need on väga hapud.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ning haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumas rasvas pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab kapsa pooleldi, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 45 minutit.
Lisa odrakruubid ja kuubikuteks lõigatud kartulid, lisa vajadusel vett ning hauta veel 40–45 minutit, kuni kruubid ja liha on pehmed.
Sega aeg-ajalt, maitsesta soola ja pipraga ning lase enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti järelevalveta: kruubid ja kapsas kleepuvad põhja ning kõrbevad kergesti.
Ära lisa kruupe ja kartuleid kohe algusest: need keevad pudruks, enne kui liha on pehme.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas ja liha annavad soolasust juba ise ning toit võib üle soolata.
output.tip: Mulgikapsad on järgmisel päeval veel paremad, sest maitsed sulavad kokku, nii et keeda neid julgelt varuga.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja loputa need kurnas enne keetmist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha poti põhjas kuumas rasvas igast küljest pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole kapsast, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1,5–2 tundi.
Kupsta ja keeda kartulid eraldi pehmeks 20 minutit enne roa valmimist ning püreesta need.
Maitsesta sool ja pipraga, sega vahepeal ning lisa vajadusel vett; serveeri kartulipudruga.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti järelvalveta ilma vett lisamata: kapsas ja kruubid kleepuvad põhja külge ning kõrbevad.
Ära soola liiga vara: hapukapsas on juba soolane ja roog võib muutuda liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda liiga kõrgel kuumusel: liha jääb kõvaks ja kruubid lähevad pudruks.
output.tip: Mulgikapsad maitsevad teisel päeval veel paremini, sest maitsed jõuavad omavahel sulanduda.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kuni alustad ülejäänud toiduga, ja nõruta enne kasutamist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumal rasval kuldpruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae veel 3–4 minutit.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole kapsast, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 30 minutit.
Lisa odrakruubid, sega läbi ja hauta veel 30–40 minutit, kuni kruubid on pehmed. Lisa vajadusel vett.
Koori ja keeda kartulid soolaga maitsestatud vees 20–25 minutit pehmeks. Serveeri mulgikapsad kartulitega.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kruupe liiga vara ega liiga vähese vedeliku sisse: nad põhjas kõrbevad ja jäävad kõvaks.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma segamata: paks toit kleepub põhja ja kõrbeb kergesti.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas on juba soolane ja roog võib minna liiga soolaseks.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis tulevad maitsed paremini kokku.

pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks (üle 5 mm): need ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja lõhe jõuab enne valmis kui kartul.
Ära pane kartuliviile ilma õlita ahjuplaadile: need kleepuvad külge, kuivavad ja jäävad kahvli all kõvaks.
Ära küpseta lõhet liiga kaua: üle 15 minutiga muutub liha kuivaks ja kuivab välja valge albumiin, mis sööb mahlakuse.
output.tip: Pane sidrunimahl lõhele alles viimasel 5 minutil või serveerimisel, siis ei hakka hape liha pealt kuivaks tegema ja maitse jääb värskem.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja lõhe on valmis enne kartuleid.
Ära pane kartuleid ilma õli ja soolata ahju: viilud kleepuvad ahjuplaadi külge ning jäävad maitsetuks ja kahvatuks.
Ära lisa sidrunimahla lõhele pikalt enne küpsetamist ega liiga rohkelt: hape muudab kala pinna kuivaks ja kõvaks.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee paberkäterätiga ja lase 10 minutit toasoojas seista enne kartulite peale panemist, siis küpseb kala ühtlasemalt ja jääb mahlasem.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksuks (üle 5 mm): 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toorest.
Ära pane kartuleid kuiva ja õlita ahjuplaadile: need kleepuvad plaadi külge ja ei saa kena kuldset koorikut.
Ära pane lõhet külmkapi külmana otse kuumadele kartulitele: pealt kuivab ära, seest jääb toorest ning küpsemisaeg venib.
output.tip: Sega kartuliviilud enne ahju 2 spl oliiviõli ja soolaga ning laota ühe kihina, siis küpsevad need ühtlaselt ja lõhe jääb mahlane.

pitfalls: Ära kalla jahu korraga vedelikku: taignasse jäävad tükid, mis ei lahustu ka seismise ajal ja pannkoogid on kogukad.
Ära pane sulatatud võid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja taigen läheb tükiliseks.
Ära küpseta pannkooke liiga kuumal pannil ega kalla taignat liiga paksult: serv kõrbeb, keskkoht jääb toorest ja koogid rebenevad keerates.
output.tip: Määri esimese pannkoogi jaoks pann kergelt võiga ja kalla taigen pannile 60–80 ml kaupa, siis saad ühtlaselt õhukesed pannkoogid ja esimene koputus näitab, kas kuumus on paigas.

pitfalls: Ära vala jahu korraga vedelikku: tainasse jäävad tombud, mida hiljem on raske lahti vispeldada.
Ära jäta esimest pannkoogi enne küpsetamist pannile määrimata ega kuumuta panni liiga kuumaks: pann kas kleepub või põleb pannkoogi alt tume ja pealt jääb toores.
Ära pööra pannkooki liiga vara: kui serv pole veel kuiv ja pind matt, rebeneb pannkook pöörates ja läheb tükkideks.
output.tip: Kalla taigen kaanega kannu või mõõtekannu, siis saad pannile valada ühtlase koguse (umbes 60–70 ml ühe pannkoogi kohta) ja pannkoogid tulevad ühesuurused.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse kuumana: see võib munad kerkima panna ja taignasse tekivad tükid, jahuta või enne veidi.
Ära küpseta liiga kõrgel kuumusel: pannkoogi äär kõrbeb ära, enne kui keskosa läbi küpseb, hoia pann keskmisel kuumusel (umbes 180 °C).
Ära keera pannkooki liiga vara: kui pind on veel läikiv ja märg, rebeneb koogi keeramisel ning jääb kleepuma.
output.tip: Määri pann esimese pannkoogi jaoks õhukeselt võiga ja järgmistele enam mitte, sest taignas on juba võid ning esimene kook näitab, kas kuumus on paigas.
